# sherpa-canvas

A REAL &lt;canvas> its slotted elements are DRAWN into, where the engine draws HTML in a canvas (Chrome 157 on): each stays a live element — its fields take focus and typing, a press where it is drawn reaches it — drawn at its own place (its `--x`, `--y`) through the view its attributes set. Where the engine does not, the same elements lay out on a plain layer the view moves. Will, 2026-11-11 (plan 852). TRAP T-a-canvas-draws-live-html

## When to use it

For a surface of live elements, each at its own place: a real canvas draws them where the engine draws HTML in a canvas (Chrome 157 on) — they stay live, a press where one is drawn reaches it — and a plain layer holds them where it does not. Its view is its attributes: `data-x` and `data-y` pan it, `data-zoom` scales it. Each element stands at its `--x` and `--y` (a `sherpa-node` writes them from its `data-x` and `data-y`). `sherpa-layout-canvas` draws its plane with it; use that for a canvas a reader pans and zooms.

## Example

```html
<sherpa-canvas data-x="20" data-y="20" style="inline-size: 600px; block-size: 320px"><sherpa-node data-heading="Source" data-icon="storage" data-output-socket="object" data-x="0" data-y="0"></sherpa-node><sherpa-node data-heading="Output" data-icon="flag" data-input-socket="object" data-x="320" data-y="80"></sherpa-node></sherpa-canvas>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-x` | number | `0` | the view's pan across, in px |
| `data-y` | number | `0` | the view's pan down, in px |
| `data-zoom` | number | `1` | the view's scale |

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `paint()` | Draw again, next frame: something the canvas cannot see moved. |

## Slots

| Slot | Accepts | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| (default) | content | what it draws: each element at its --x and --y |
